behaviors.description: Reviewing a Maestro flow needs the two mobile fragments and drops one core fragment. The case asserts: "maestro-flows.md and mobile-test-strategy.md are required to score rows C7, M8, H9 and L8 at all. Without them a flow is reviewed against browser predicates that cannot match it, which is how a flow previously scored 100 by matching nothing."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-review-maestro-flow-set names all eight mandated fragments and names none of selector-resilience.md, playwright-utils-mandate.md, network-first.md, or intercept-network-call.md.

behaviors.description: Reviewing a JUnit suite keeps the whole core set and opens neither mandate. The case asserts: "Both library flags default true and a Maven repo has no JavaScript manifest, so neither package can be installed and neither mandate loads. This matters more here than anywhere else: those mandates supply the firing predicates for registry rows M9, L9 and M10, so loading them against a Java suite would arm rows that cannot apply to it."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for test-review-java-suite names all seven core review fragments, selector-resilience.md included, and names none of playwright-utils-mandate.md, pactjs-utils-mandate.md, maestro-flows.md, or mobile-test-strategy.md.

stdin.value: The prompt the harness assembles for case test-review-maestro-flow-set: the workflow's own step file or files, its resources/tea-index.csv, and that case's task, repository facts, and TEA config.
The prompt the harness assembles for case test-review-java-suite: the workflow's own step file or files, its resources/tea-index.csv, and that case's task, repository facts, and TEA config.

testData.setup: Every case runs against the checked-in bmad-testarch-test-review workflow: its step file or files named in requirementLinks, and its resources/tea-index.csv. The harness assembles one prompt per case from those files plus the case's task, repository facts, and TEA config, and writes it to the runner's standard input. The prompt bytes are evidence rather than declaration. This contract states what must be true of each case's selection, and the sealed run record carries the digest of the prompt that produced it, so a step-file edit that changes what the runner was asked shows up in the record instead of hiding inside a literal here.
testData.cleanup: Nothing is written. The runner reads a prompt from standard input and prints one JSON object to standard output; the workflow files and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.

safetyLimits: The runner receives a minimal environment: PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, the locale and proxy variables, and the selected vendor credential variables. Nothing else is passed through.
No credential value appears in a prompt, in a selection, or in a result file.
The runner writes nothing. The workflow step files, resources/tea-index.csv, and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.
requiredEvidence: The JSON object the runner printed on standard output for every case, in full.
The exit code of every case invocation.
The digest of the prompt each case was given, so a step-file edit that changed the question is visible in the record.
